The afferent intensity scalar field models how internal muscular feedback constrains action execution, forming a scalar-valued function I(M) where M indexes muscle groups. This scalar field acts as a constraint in GSE’s state-space optimization, guiding transitions between motor states. The will strength guidance primitive posits that volition modulates intensity rather than direction, enabling a Bayesian interpretation where W(T) represents a latent variable influencing action variance. The sensory image primitive links pre-movement cognition to post-execution outcomes, suggesting that GSE must encode sensory templates as part of its planning kernel. These primitives form a dual structure: one grounded in physical sensation (afferent), the other in cognitive anticipation (intent). Their interaction defines a closed-loop system where sensory feedback refines future intentions, creating a recursive refinement mechanism. Failure modes include loss of sensory fidelity leading to inaccurate intensity estimation, or absence of sensory imagery causing intent ambiguity. In both cases, the system degrades into stochastic behavior without proper grounding in either internal or external reference frames.
